阿丽亚娜·格兰德（Ariana Grande）正在戏弄一个以她的“永恒阳光巡演”为中心的孔雀项目，该项目可能是一部纪录片或音乐会电影。

这位歌手的巡演片段被发布在社交媒体上，显示她站在舞台中央演唱《永恒的阳光》。当视频逐渐变黑时，屏幕上的文字写着：“即将推出……孔雀。”

Ariana Grande is teasing a Peacock project centered on her Eternal Sunshine Tour that could be a documentary or concert film.

A clip of the singer was posted on social media from her tour, showing her standing in the middle of the stage and singing “Eternal Sunshine.” As the clip fades to black, text on screen reads, “Coming soon to… Peacock.”

“I don’t care what people say it’s true, say it’s true,” Grande is heard singing in the clip shared on Instagram by the NBCUniversal streaming platform and the singer.

Arianators were already on the case and suspected the singer was working on something after Grande posted a photo on social media last week alongside director Christian Breslauer and editor Andrew Morrow. Breslauer worked with Grande on videos like “Yes, and?” and “We Can’t Be Friends (Wait for Your Love,” while Morrow is known for editing Beyoncé’s Renaissance: A Film by Beyoncé.

Grande toured Canada, England, and the U.S. with the Eternal Sunshine Tour earlier this year, kicking things off on June 6 at the Oakland Arena in Oakland. The singer would then travel to the Los Angeles area to perform six shows between Crypto.com Arena and the Kia Forum. Other cities Grande stopped in included Austin, Atlanta, New York City, Chicago, Boston, and Montreal. Grande ended her tour at The O2 Arena in London, England, performing 10 shows, with her last performance on September 1st.

Currently, Grande is in the middle of promoting her latest film, Focker-in-Law, in which she stars alongside Ben Stiller, Skyler Gisondo, Owen Wilson, Robert De Niro, and more. The comedy film opens in theaters on November 25.

items.content:
中新网天津11月24日电(江艳优 文思涵) 叶嘉莹先生逝世两周年之际，南开大学沈立岩教授日前接受中新网专访。访谈立足亲历受教的追忆，探讨如何将叶嘉莹先生独树一帜的精神魅力，转化为可感知、可参与的公众文化实践，并探寻新时代语境下中华诗教的传承路径。针对这一系列兼具学术价值与现实意义的议题，沈立岩教授作出深度阐释。

“年轻的时候听叶先生讲课，只觉得内容生动、旁征博引，佩服得不得了。但真正读懂她说的那些话，是人生过半以后的事。”面对当下追求即时反馈的快节奏，沈立岩回望恩师的诗教事业，看见了一种截然不同的特质：诗教是时间的艺术，今日播下的种子，往往要等到半生之后，才传来的回响。

沈立岩的亲身经历，便是对这份“延迟”最好的注脚。他以屈原的《橘颂》为例：“年轻时只觉得写得漂亮、热闹，后来才真正体会到‘行比伯夷，置以为像兮’的分量，懂得了其中个人、家族与国家之间不可分割的血缘联系。”

岁月向前，人世的聚散起落一一降临，年少时积累的词句不断翻上心头。这也印证了叶先生诗教的内核：把诗句收纳进记忆，如同埋下种子。亲历劳作，才读懂悲悯；饱尝漂泊，才懂得望月怀人的乡愁。这份贯通古今的情感共鸣，正是诗词的生命力所在。

“她对文化的一往情深，这是没办法表演的。”谈及叶嘉莹身上最难被复制的特点，沈立岩说道，“情感到达了那里，就自然会流露。”讲课的节奏、引经据典的方式，这些表面的形迹，通过备课积累或者借助科技也许能加以传承；但叶先生对中华文化的那份“深情”，却需要教育工作者持之以恒的体悟与沉淀。为了长久保留这份真情，南开大学相关项目正利用数字影像技术还原叶先生讲诗的声音和形象，探索诗教数字化平台。

技术的介入，让大师的智慧得以更轻量地抵达公众。而在沈立岩看来，中国人血脉里天然就有诗性的文化基因，没有人真正远离诗词。当下，古典诗词在短视频平台上频频爆火，像“欲买桂花同载酒”这类诗句引发网友共鸣。学术界常有担忧，认为这种碎片化的理解会消解经典，但沈立岩十分笃定：“诗它是全方位的，不需要过多设限。中华诗教的根基足够强大，经得起时代多样的解读。”在沈立岩看来，不论是学术性解读还是娱乐化传播，只要“永远都记得有诗在”就好。网络制造的热闹让诗词迅速抵达年轻人眼前，这未尝不是一种很好的相遇。

然而，相遇只是开始。为了让这些因偶然相遇而心生兴趣的年轻人有真正扎根的土壤，沈立岩带领的南开团队在背后做着极其扎实的“慢功夫”。在文献研究方面，团队正牵头整理中华诗教文献集成，系统汇集了从先秦到清末的历代诗教史料，填补了此前相关文献缺乏汇集整理的空白。在课程建设上，入选教育部原创教材培育项目的《中华诗教概论》已配套开设线上通识课及校内微专业，后续还将编写《中华诗教史》。此外，在南开大学前沿交叉科学研究院重点项目“中华诗教与中华文化传播”的支持下，团队还与短视频平台合作，推出唐诗相关的传播内容并配套出版普及读物。

“我们要把这些浩瀚的文献，做成大众和中小学教师能看懂的精简读本，这才是薪火相传的坚实基础。”沈立岩深知，这项事业并不渴求立竿见影的成果。留住中国人代代相传的精神底色，让今人依然能够听见千年前古人的心声，本就是一场漫长的修行。

如果要用一个词形容对叶先生的事业的延续，沈立岩选择了“薪火相传”。正如叶先生所写“师弟因缘逾骨肉，书生志意托讴吟。”师生之间因诗词结缘，感情甚至超越了骨肉亲情，共同的志向就是把诗教传下去。

在访谈最后，沈立岩又以灯火作喻，诠释这份薪火的意义：“纵使周遭沉入无边黑暗，只要你手中还握着一盏灯，那就不能让它就此熄灭，要让它一直亮下去，再去点亮更多的灯。”

items.content:
中新网天津11月24日电(陈玥汐 宋蕊婷)“只要有诗的地方，就有诗教。”在短视频平台上，一些年轻人把叶嘉莹先生讲诗的片段放在视频开头，随后配上自己写下的文字，分享各自的阅读感受和生活体会，以此表达对文学的热爱，收获数万点赞。在叶嘉莹先生逝世两周年之际，国家社会科学基金重大项目“中华诗教文献集成与理论研究”首席专家、南开大学文学院教授沈立岩接受采访，深情回顾了与叶先生的往事，并深入剖析诗教理念与其当代价值。

年轻人用新的模式在互联网上分享自己对古典诗词的热爱，诗教以润物无声的方式，持续走进普通人的生活。“这是一种榜样的力量，就像古代有孔子，后人可以照着他学、跟着他说、接着他做。”沈立岩分析了此类视频的内在逻辑，年轻人首先被叶先生的讲诗视频打动，产生个人与诗的共鸣，借此来讲述自身的经历体会，这种现象正是叶嘉莹先生精神影响的生动体现。

谈及这类视频表达与诗教的联系，沈立岩认为，这类创作新颖呈现出诗教的潜移默化作用，并能引发更为广泛的文学讨论。在他看来，诗教并不局限于课堂之上，也不以专业知识为门槛。一个人翻开一本《唐诗三百首》，因其中的某句诗而有所触动，诗教便可能已经发生。如果一首诗能够在不同的人生阶段唤起新的感受，也能够让千年前的情感抵达今天，那么，这种感动自然不应只属于具有专业文学背景的人。沈立岩指出，普通人既可以是诗教的对象，也可以成为诗教的主体。“不是所有的人都有诗才，但是很多人实际上是有诗情的。”一个人或许没有接受过专业的诗词教育，却仍可能在某个时刻，因为一句诗而重新理解自己的生活。

诗歌具有优美的语言、和谐的声韵、丰富的情感、深刻的思想、生动的形象、高远的境界，能够对人产生全方位的影响，其作用效果远远超过通过讲述概念进行的一般教育。从古至今，人类的情感始终有许多共通之处，随着人生阅历的不断丰富，诗歌会在某一刻与人产生精神上的同频共振，这便是兴发感动。沈立岩以唐代诗人孟浩然诗作《春晓》为例，诗人以简洁的笔触将读者带入千年前的情景，雨后清晨鸟声清越悠扬，当下的鸟鸣令人回想起夜间风雨、繁花飘零。诗人由对花鸟的关心引发对生命的思考与关切，看似简单的诗句，蕴含了人对宇宙间生命节律和周期的体验。“叶先生能够体会这种情感，并把它讲出来。”沈立岩有感而发，“我一想到这些，就对人生的意义价值，对宇宙、自然，对其它的生命多了一层敬畏。”诗能通过情感教育、道德教育、审美教育、社会教育等方面，产生人生观、价值观、宇宙观整体的熏陶，起到“润物细无声”的深刻影响。

在现代社会，诗教的现实价值愈发清晰。沈立岩提出，“诗歌是重要的媒介，因为诗是情感的存在。”情感能帮人锚定归处，不被效率、流量等裹挟，而文学艺术正是人类情感的结晶。他引用墨子的“亲知”理论，指出只有具身体会才能真正理解概念，“人工智能在当下盛行，但它们始终没有情感，即使知道‘情感’这一概念，却永远无法切实体验。”诗歌通过语言、声韵与意象，让人得以体察自身的喜怒哀乐，感受那些无法被简单概念化的生命经验，这一份独属于人的兴发感动，正是叶嘉莹先生穷尽一生想要传递的东西。

这种丰富的情感，往往能穿透现实的壁垒，实现跨越时空的思想交流。叶嘉莹先生曾听说蓝鲸可以隔洋传语，由此写下“遗音沧海如能会，便是千秋共此时”。古人写下的诗，就像沧海之中留下的一声鸣叫、传扬万里，只要真正用心去体会，总有一天，读过的东西能跟自己的精神达到共鸣。当那一刻到来时，一瞬间便穿越了时间空间的距离，和古人有了精神上的交流。“好像他在直接对你说话，而你这一刻也可以直接跟他说话一样。”

那些凝结在古典诗词中的情感与理想，构成了中华文化绵延至今的重要精神资源。诗教让一代代人得以通过诗歌，重新理解自己、理解他人，也与共同的文化传统建立联系。

Zosia Mamet recently revealed that her “absolutely horrible” experience working with showrunner and producer Matthew Weiner on the set of “Mad Men” caused her to quit the series after just five episodes.

“All the other actors were wonderful, but he really was like the Catholic Church back in the day, like that bro rules with fear,” she said while appearing on Dax Shepard’s “Armchair Expert” podcast on Monday. “He would dart every table read with this little speech… and he would talk about how he didn’t want any of us to take our scripts home… And he would be like, ‘If I see that, I’m going to find you, and I’m going to hunt you down. I’m going to kill you. Just kidding. Actually not. He would do this at every table read. And I was like, this not only isn’t funny, but it’s yucky. It’s fucking yucky, man.”

Mamet, who appeared on Season 4 and 5 of the hit drama as Joyce Ramsay, then recounted the moment that pushed her to quit the show, explaining that “he came in and was having a bad day and decided to set his sights on me.” “During a block rehearsal, [he] just fucking went to town on me in front of the whole cast and crew… I called my agents when I left, and I was like, ‘I can’t go back to that set,’” she told Shepard. “He just systematically dressed me down for like 45 minutes. And I was like, ‘I want to kill myself.’”

She continued: “My level of insecurity was so great that I knew that I wouldn’t be able [to]. I was like, I will shut down,” Mamet said. “I won’t be able to function in this environment, and the fear of that happening again was just too great.”

The “Girls” actress had previously written about the showrunner in her 2025 essay collection, “Does This Make Me Funny?,” though she didn’t name him at the time. “I wrote an essay about it for my book where I don’t mention names,” Mamet said. “But I really wanted Matt Weiner to sue me because then he would be admitting to the fact that he knew I was writing about him.”

Reps for Weiner did not immediately respond to Variety’s request for comment.

一小时后，罗森塔尔声称福卡和他的一行人仍然站在酒吧的队伍外，在注意到他们的存在后，福卡走近并被指控向他的女儿喷胡椒喷雾。当经理否认这一指控时，福卡“掏出手枪”并“打”了罗森塔尔的脸，然后对罗森塔尔进行了“种族和反犹太主义诽谤”，并威胁“要杀了他”。

“Michael” director Antoine Fuqua has been accused of assault, battery and intentional infliction of emotional distress by a Los Angeles bar manager following an incident back in February during which Fuqua allegedly pulled a gun on and struck the employee in the head.

In a 10-page civil claim filed Friday in the Los Angeles Superior Court, William Rosenthal, an assistant manager at the bar Good Times at Davey Wayne’s, is said to have denied entry to Fuqua, his son, Brando, and his daughter because they were “visibly overly intoxicated.” Rosenthal was then spat on by a member of the group, to which Rosenthal told them they needed to leave the bar.

An hour later, Rosenthal alleges that Fuqua and his party remained standing outside the bar’s line, and upon noticing their presence, was approached by Fuqua and accused of pepper-spraying his daughter. When the manager denied the allegation, Fuqua “pulled out a handgun” and “struck” Rosenthal in the face before directing “a racial and antisemitic slur” at Rosenthal and threatening “to kill him.”

“As Plaintiff staggered back in pain, Defendant Brando Fuqua appeared and approached Plaintiff and forcefully swung a handgun at Plaintiff’s face,” read the complaint. “Defendants Antoine Fuqua and Brandon Fuqua then pointed their handguns at Plaintiff, placing him in imminent fear for his life, before fleeing down the street.”

Rosenthal is seeking $50,000 as a result of his suffering “serious physical and psychological injuries” which include a nose fracture, head injury, skin lacerations, post-traumatic stress disorder, severe emotional distress and severe scarring, all of which continue to cause him “great physical and mental pain and suffering.” The claim noted that Rosenthal believes said injuries “will result in some permanent disability.”

Reps for Fuqua did not immediately respond to Variety‘s request for comment.

东北书写其来有自。从萧红、萧军等为代表的东北作家群以来，对东北这片土地的观照接续不断，是现当代文艺的重要组成。梁晓声2017年出版的长篇小说《人世间》及其同名电视剧，通过东北某城市家庭的生活变迁展现时代变迁，写出了一部温情而又厚重的年代史。持续播出20年的系列电视剧《乡村爱情》，将东北乡土叙事的美学风格发挥到极致。这些老少咸宜的生活化叙事，挫折下有情义，幽默中有温暖，是东北叙事的基本面。

而过去10余年里，青年创作者在继承的基础上有所创新，掀起一股横跨小说、电影、剧集的叙事潮流，产生广泛影响。电影《钢的琴》《白日焰火》，小说《平原上的摩西》《冬泳》，剧集《漫长的季节》《胆小鬼》等，不同文艺形式之间相互影响、交叉改编，形成了鲜明的艺术风格，放大了东北叙事的声势。

工厂里沉默的烟囱，缓慢降落的大雪，枯草与铁锈，青春、命运与承担，结尾处戛然而止的爆裂，最终如命运般归于平静。这类东北叙事，融入类型元素，借助悬疑小说的套路，以悬念牢牢抓住受众胃口。需要指出的是，悬疑不是故弄玄虚，而是贴合着人物命运的曲折，展现一个人无论陷于怎样的困境，最终依然是有尊严地捍卫着生活。

在艺术手法创新之外，这批作品同样贴近当下青年的新关切与新情绪，概括地说，和新大众文艺的宗旨一致，都是展现平凡生活的价值。过往“成功学”的框架，以单一的发展标准来指认地域或个体，有时会遮蔽掉平凡人生的意义，甚至将“平凡”错误地理解为“失败”。这批青年创作者拿出的东北故事，有力扭转了这一偏见，让人们正视平凡的意义与价值。

从这一视角看，如今，东北叙事跳出悬疑的单一类型，把镜头从往事拉向当下，也是想进一步贴近当下青年的情绪与情感。在《小城良方》中，从东北来到南方三甲医院工作的青年才俊，患有罕见的“恐雪症”，这既是主人公青年时代的心理创伤，同时也是一处微妙的隐喻。电视剧的线索，可以理解为主人公如何回到故乡执业，在东北小城中疗愈自己的精神病灶。

由此能看到，东北叙事之所以长热不衰，很大程度上在于“东北”是一种平衡。以往东北叙事重要的创作者迟子建，其作品《额尔古纳河右岸》等之所以受欢迎，正在于以自然的形态提供了一种都市的平衡。与之相比，《小城良方》《蒸蒸日上》等作品不是着力于渲染草原雪山，而是以小城平衡大城，以踏踏实实的日常平衡高处不胜寒的焦虑。

各地这么多小城，为什么偏偏是东北的小城叙事走出来了？原因或许在于，东北的小城并不是真正的“小”，而是有前史，有故事，有起起伏伏的经历，也有过尽千帆的淡然。这样的小城，能安放人生和心灵，让一切荣辱浮沉，沉淀回生活本身。归来的无论是医生还是律师，都会被洋溢着烟火气的生活以及带着喜剧感的东北话所疗愈。

时代在加速，高强度的竞争给人们带来身心压力。而这些鲜活的东北故事及其讲述，回应着我们的生活，慰藉着我们的心灵，提供一种来自文艺的平衡。

独家报道：格雷格·霍瓦尼西安（《迷雾》、《红衣主教》）和林赛·诺明顿（《玛戈的金钱烦恼》、《阿诺拉》）将主演新心理惊悚片《夜浪》，该片由克里斯蒂安·麦凯（《请勿打开》、《杀戮之旅》）编剧兼导演，Obscura Film 编剧。切丽·柯里（《狐狸》、《暮光之城：电影》）和肖恩·科菲（《美少女的谎言》、《好女孩》）也将出演。

《夜浪》以德克萨斯州黑暗、荒凉的高速公路为背景，在一个晚上的时间里展开，讲述了一个独自开车的年轻人梅森（霍瓦内西安饰）的故事，他与一位神秘女子（诺明顿饰）意外的电话交谈提供了最初令人欢迎的逃离。当他们的交流从调情转向越来越令人不安的问题时，电话那头的女人开始威胁梅森拼命想要解决的一切问题。

柯里和科菲的角色目前处于保密状态。

目前正在圣安东尼奥和德克萨斯州周边地区进行制作。

EXCLUSIVE: Greg Hovanessian (The Mist, Cardinal) and Lindsey Normington (Margo’s Got Money Troubles, Anora) are set to lead the new psychological thriller Nightwaves, from writer and director Kristian McKay (Do Not Open, Kill Trip) and Obscura Film. Cherie Currie (Foxes, Twilight Zone: The Movie) and Shane Coffey (Pretty Little Liars, Good Girls) will also star.

Set against the dark, desolate highways of Texas, Nightwaves unfolds over the course of a single night, following Mason (Hovanessian), a young man driving alone whose unexpected phone conversation with a mysterious woman (Normington) offers an initially welcome escape. As their exchange shifts from flirtation to increasingly unsettling questions, the woman on the other end of the line begins to threaten everything Mason is desperately trying to leave behind. With each passing mile, he finds himself moving closer to a confrontation he cannot simply hang up to avoid.

Currie and Coffey’s roles are under wraps.

Production is currently underway in San Antonio and the surrounding Texas landscape.

“There’s something incredibly intimate about talking to someone in the dark when you can’t see their face. You start filling in the blanks, and that can be seductive or terrifying,” shared McKay. “With Nightwaves, I want the audience to feel that connection tightening until it becomes a trap. Greg and Lindsey bring the vulnerability and unpredictability these roles demand, and having Cherie and Shane in this world gives the film such a distinct personality.”

Obscura Film touts in a release how “McKay will bring a distinctive visual approach to the thriller, allowing tension and performances to unfold in extended, uninterrupted moments. Using the empty stretches of highway, passing headlights, and the confined interior of a moving car, the film transforms an ordinary phone conversation into an increasingly claustrophobic psychological experience, where what remains unseen may be more terrifying than anything in view.”

The film is produced by Obscura Film partners Daunesh Alcott and McKay, alongside Jose Corres. Executive produced by Gustavo Oliveira.

Nightwaves expands Obscura Film’s growing slate of independently produced genre features. The project follows Kill Trip, acquired by Quiver Distribution and released in 2026, and Do Not Open, McKay’s supernatural thriller starring Freddy Carter, Lulu Wilson, Mark McKenna, John Ford Coley and Stelio Savante, which is currently in post-production.

Earth’s Mightiest Heroes will fight Doctor Doom in the latest Avengers installment, but they won’t face the first wave of critics and major guilds on the awards calendar.

Marvel Studios’ “Avengers: Doomsday” will not screen for awards voting bodies before its world premiere, Variety has learned exclusively, a move designed to protect its theatrical run by keeping the film’s closely guarded plot turns out of the spoiler ecosystem ahead of its Dec. 18 theatrical release. The film premieres Dec. 14 in Los Angeles, just four days before it opens nationwide.

The strategy follows a well-worn playbook for event films of this scale, from “Star Wars: The Force Awakens” to “Spider-Man: No Way Home.” But protecting the surprises comes at a cost, with “Doomsday” set to sit out a long stretch of the precursor season as voting windows close before most awards voters have seen a frame. The biggest question is: What does that mean for the Oscars?

The most consequential window belongs to the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences. Preliminary voting for the Oscar shortlists begins Monday, Dec. 7, and closes Dec. 11, with shortlists in 12 categories announced on Dec. 15, the day after the film’s premiere. Those categories are animated short film, casting, cinematography, documentary feature, documentary short, international feature, live action short, makeup and hairstyling, original score, original song, sound and visual effects. “Doomsday” could factor into as many as seven of them.

Visual effects is where “Doomsday” has the clearest path because of how that race is structured, and the studio’s previous successes in the category (i.e., “Guardians of the Galaxy,” “Black Panther: Wakanda Forever”). Before the official 10-film shortlist is announced Dec. 15, the field is narrowed to 20 semifinalists, a list the Academy does not make public, though Variety has reported it exclusively in past seasons. That list is expected to take shape in the coming days.

Under current Academy rules, the president appoints a chair to preside over an executive committee of active and life members of the Visual Effects Branch. That committee reviews a list of eligible films and, through a series of meetings, selects up to 20 for further consideration. Achievements are judged on “the contribution the visual effects make to the overall production” and “the human artistry and skill, fidelity and technical achievement with which the visual illusions are achieved.”

Crucially, the rules build in flexibility that limits the risk of a major spoiler leak. The executive committee “will request that producers provide opportunities to view their films through advance screenings,” and if a film isn’t available two weeks before the selection meeting, excerpts may be submitted instead. If suitable materials aren’t made available, the committee can deem the film ineligible.

It’s not clear whether Marvel Studios screened the full film for the committee or submitted excerpts. Nonetheless, Variety has confirmed that “Doomsday” was submitted to the relevant Academy branches for consideration, along with the materials required for shortlist eligibility.

In other words, a far smaller group viewing a controlled screening or a curated reel gives Marvel a way to stay in the VFX conversation without exposing its third act to hundreds of voters (The Visual Effects Branch is among the top five largest of the Academy). That matters for a studio that has landed visual effects nominations for “Avengers: Infinity War,” “Avengers: Endgame” and “Spider-Man: No Way Home” but is still searching for its first win in the category.

In Variety’s most recent Oscar predictions, “Avengers: Doomsday” is among the early projected five film visual effects nominees alongside “Dune: Part Three,” “Project Hail Mary” and “Wildwood.”

Adam Driver and Steven Soderbergh didn’t get paid for the two-and-a-half years they spent developing “The Hunt for Ben Solo,” a standalone “Star Wars” movie that would’ve centered on Driver’s fan favorite character Kylo Ren/Ben Solo. The actor said on the “Talk Easy” podcast that money was not even top of mind since they were given the upmost assurance from then-Lucasfilm president Kathleen Kennedy that the movie would happen, and thus the pay of it all could be figured out once it was greenlit.

“We were gonna do a Ben Solo movie and that didn’t happen. And we worked on it for a long time,” Driver said on the podcast. “Soderbergh did that for nothing, because we were given a lot of confidence. Like Kathy [Kennedy] said we have a 100% approval rate [from Disney]. We worked on it. No one’s paying us to work on it. The only reason we were working on it was we fucking loved the idea, how we wanted to do it, and I loved that character. And that was it. That was our guiding principle. All the money stuff came later. We were trying to figure out how to make it cheap so they could let us do what we wanted to do. So that was kind of a bummer.”

Driver revealed the existence of “The Hunt for Ben Solo” in an October 2025 interview with The Associated Press, explaining how Disney executives pulled the plug on the project because they couldn’t wrap their heads around the character coming back after he presumably died in 2019’s “Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker.”

“I always was interested in doing another ‘Star Wars,’” Driver said at the time. “I had been talking about doing another one since 2021. Kathleen [Kennedy] had reached out. I always said: ‘With a great director and a great story, I’d be there in a second.’ I loved that character and loved playing him.”

In an AP interview earlier this month, Driver said it was “criminal” for Disney to scrap “The Hunt for Ben Solo” after also saying on “The Rich Eisen Show” around the same time that the project is officially dead and he has no interest in trying to revive it (“I think the ship has sailed though,” Driver said).

“For me it was: Steven Soderbergh wants to make a ‘Star Wars’ film. What are we debating?” Driver told AP. “It’s what it is. It’s criminal. Or it felt criminal. We’re all moving on. On to the next. And Steven already has something else that’s one of the best things he’s ever written.”

Driver originally told the AP in 2025 that he loved “The Hunt for Ben Solo” script, calling it the “standard” of what a “Star Wars” movie “should be” and comparing it to the “handmade and character-driven” feel of “The Empire Strikes Back.” He added that Lucasfilm execs Kennedy, Dave Filoni and Cary Beck backed the project until Disney shut it down.

“We presented the script to Lucasfilm. They loved the idea,” Driver recalled. “They totally understood our angle and why we were doing it. We took it to Bob Iger and Alan Bergman, and they said no. They didn’t see how Ben Solo was alive. And that was that.”

Kathleen Kennedy expressed her own frustration with Disney pulling the plug on the project during her Lucasfilm exit interview. Soderbergh told BK Mag soon after that he was not surprised to read about Kennedy’s annoyances.

“We were all frustrated,” Soderbergh said. “You know, that was two and a half years of free work for me and Adam and [writer] Rebecca Blunt. When Adam and I discussed him talking about it publicly, I said, ‘Look, do not editorialize or speculate about the why. Just say what happened, because all we know is what happened.’ The stated reason was, ‘We don’t think Ben Solo could be alive.’ And that was all we were told. And so there’s nothing to do about it, you know, except move on.”

items.originalContent:
Peermusic has signed a publishing deal for the song catalog of Gram Parsons and will assume worldwide administration, it was announced last week by Peermusic CEO Mary Megan Peer and U.S./ Canada president Jamie Cerreta. Perhaps more than any other artist, Parsons — who was inducted posthumously into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame on November 14 — was responsible for the country-rock fusion that has spawned everything from the music of the Eagles to the entire Americana genre. His influence was obvious in a showcase held earlier this month at his old haunt, the Troubador in Los Angeles, featuring his musical collaborator Emmylou Harris, as well as Elvis Costello, the Black Crowes, and Margo Price.

Polly Parsons said: “My father’s music has always had a life of its own, reaching across generations and continuing to inspire artists and listeners in ways I don’t think even he could have imagined. It means so much to me to help preserve that legacy while also finding new ways for people to discover his songs. His music was never bound by genre or convention, and I think that’s why it still resonates so deeply today. My hope is that this new partnership will not only honor the incredible body of work he left behind but also introduce his music to a whole new generation of fans. Keeping his spirit and his songs alive is something I hold very close to my heart.”

Jamie Cerreta commented: “Gram’s music is an enduring testament to how great songs remain in our hearts. All of us at Peermusic are so honored to represent his songs and to see his work celebrated through his recent induction into the Rock n Roll Hall of Fame. I am personally so happy to be working with Polly and Vector Management to help another generation discover the greatness of Gram Parsons.”

+ The Songwriters Hall of Fame has announced the posthumous induction of legendary singer-songwriter Roger Miller, known for such hits at “King of the Road” and “Dang Me.” Miller, who died in 1992 at age 56, was honored during an intimate ceremony held November 17, 2026, at BMI headquarters on Music Row in Nashville.

Miller’s widow Mary said: “We were ecstatic to learn that Roger was being inducted into the Songwriters Hall of Fame. Of all his many talents, he was most proud of his songwriting. This lifetime achievement would have meant a great deal to him, and we are honored to celebrate the recognition of his extraordinary body of work.”

+ Ignacio Meyer has been named president of Universal Music Latin America & Iberian Peninsula, effective immediately. He will report to Felipe Holguin, who was named CEO of the division last week. Meyer has held leadership roles at TelevisaUnivision since 2011. Most recently he was president of its U.S. Networks & Local Media; previously, he founded and served as managing partner of advisory firm Konexxion Enterprises, worked as an artist manager and served on the management team of IFPI Latin America.

Holguin said: “Artists are at the heart of how we’re building this next chapter. Nacho combines creative sensibility and strategic vision with a deep understanding of how to nurture each artist’s individuality, grow their audience, and heighten their impact across platforms. He’ll add a powerful dimension to our leadership team as we invest in extraordinary artists and bring bold ideas to life. We know from experience how well we work together, and I’m delighted to welcome him to UMG.”

+ Americana award-winning artist Nathaniel Rateliff has signed with Red Light Management’s Will Botwin and Coran Capshaw for representation. Rateliff recently marked his 10th straight year performing at Farm Aid after being unanimously appointed to the Farm Aid board of directors; performed at Tom Morello’s inaugural Power to the People festival alongside Bruce Springsteen, Dave Matthews and Morello; and he closed this year’s Newport Folk Festival alongside Matthews, Joan Baez and more with his Nathaniel Rateliff & Friends set.

+ Warner Records has signed 21-year-old Brazilian-Mexican-American singer Lambb and released her second EP, “There’s Someone in the Yard,” last week. The singer, born Julie Gaeta, combines indie singer-songwriter approach with house and techno, and last summer performed at the Reading Festival and Leeds Festival in England as part of her first headlining tour.

+ Position Music has signed Grammy-nominated artist and songwriter Masego to a worldwide publishing deal. Masego recently released his third album, “Fix Your Face,” and was signed to Position Music by Delmar Powell, VP of A&R for the company.
